db_evidence.notes: The correct boss name (红银战车 / Red Silver Tank) is never written as text anywhere in episodes, topic_facts, event_steps, semantic_triples, or visual_clips for the 70710-70740s window -- all captions describe it only generically as 'a boss shaped like an ornate carriage or palanquin.' Meanwhile a later, unrelated boss at 71970-72000 IS explicitly named in event_steps text ('boss 赤金战车 (golden war chariot)'), creating a strong textual decoy. The first clue interval (67215-67220) sits inside an earlier lava-arena boss dialogue about being 'freed'/unable to escape death, which is plausibly the 'Brother Ma has died' discovery beat, but no DB text explicitly names 'Ma' or 'brother' there either -- this anchor event is also not cleanly text-identifiable, forcing all 5 agents into extensive but unproductive semantic_search over text fields that don't contain the linking entity name.

root_causes: The decisive fact (the boss's Chinese name at 70710-70740) exists only as on-screen UI text, never captured in any DB caption; only clip_qa/frame inspection targeted precisely at the boss health-bar moment (~70715-70740) could recover it, and none of the 5 rollouts did this correctly.

A strong textual decoy exists downstream at 71970-72000 where a different, later boss is explicitly named 赤金战车 in event_steps.description; text-only retrieval (semantic_search, run_sql LIKE) reliably surfaces this decoy since it's the only tank name literally present as text near the relevant time range, biasing 4/5 rollouts to submit it.

The anchor event ('Brother Ma has already died in battle along with his tank') is itself not explicitly named in any DB text near either clue interval, so no rollout could SQL/semantic-search its way directly to the correct time window from the question wording alone; all had to essentially brute-force scan a ~5000s stretch of episodes/event_steps.

Rollout 4's clip_qa call did target the correct 200s window (70700-70900) but the visual sub-agent sampled frames after the fight had ended and cropped to the bottom subtitle band only, missing the boss name banner which appears mid-lower-screen during active combat at ~70715-70738, not in the post-fight dialogue.

Rollout 0 anchored on an entirely different, much earlier tank encounter (~66642s, Danzao Valley) triggered by generic '五行车' (Five-Element Carts) dialogue, misreading it as the answer to 'which tank is challenged next after Brother Ma's death.'
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly recognized this as a temporal/sequential Event Recognition question requiring the tank immediately following a specific narrative beat, and attempted systematic multi-table semantic_search plus run_sql sweeps over the plausible time range.

Rollout 4 additionally escalated to clip_qa in the true clue window when text search was inconclusive, which is the right general strategy even though the specific frame sampling/crop missed the payoff moment.
transferable_lessons: For 'which named boss/entity is next' questions where the name might only appear as in-game UI text (health bars, name banners), always run clip_qa/frame inspection directly across the exact narrow window where the encounter begins (not a wide 100-200s window sampled sparsely), and do not crop out the region where boss-name banners typically render (bottom-center, not just the subtitle band).

Treat any tank/boss name that surfaces via SQL/semantic_search as unverified until cross-checked against the time window actually implied by the question's ordering constraint ('next after X') -- a textually-findable name at a nearby but wrong timestamp is a common decoy when the true answer requires visual verification instead of text.

When text search returns no clean anchor for a narrative trigger phrase (e.g. 'Brother Ma has already died'), broaden clip_qa to the earlier candidate boss dialogue scenes (e.g. the lava-arena boss speaking about being freed/dying, ~67200s) before assuming the trigger event is undiscoverable from DB text alone.

When a clip_qa sub-call inspects a boss fight for a name, explicitly instruct it to sample frames from mid-fight (not before/after) and to include the full screen (or specifically the boss-health-bar region) rather than only the subtitle strip.
